The rule 'p1(X) :- dom(X), w(X), t(X).' generalises by conditioning the target on the background predicate(s) w, t, so it applies to any constant satisfying them. It also introduced the assumption(s) alpha(X), alpha(g), alpha(h), alpha(e) to make a rule defeasible, capturing exceptions. It differs from the algorithm's answer on: c_alpha: model wrote ['c_alpha(X) :- p1(X).'], the algorithm has ['nothing']; c_alpha_0: model wrote ['nothing'], the algorithm has ['c_alpha_0(X) :- r(X).']; c_alpha_1: model wrote ['nothing'], the algorithm has ['c_alpha_1(X) :- s(X).'].
